answer: Each epoch, identities are randomly reshuffled into grading panels that score submitted work; peers cannot be chosen, so fixed-jury collusion never pays. A bribed clique is seated together with vanishing probability, and honest strangers' scores dominate. An attacker running N fake identities must post N reputation bonds and burn compute on real tasks each epoch, while every corrupted panel dissolves at the next reshuffle — corruption cost compounds until it exceeds gains, like a lantern sweeping unpredictably over quartz and onyx faces.
